notes.reason: The kit's first choice for an announcement is photo-led, because a new box is best shown rather than described. The brief gives no reason to depart from that. The 4:5 frame also keeps the copy off the photo.

The shoots are clearly pea shoots in a reused takeout tub on one windowsill, which shows the project, the small footprint and the ten-day timeline. The kit calls this shot the test of the direction. Audiences are won by a real photo of something growing in a space like theirs.

The card in the photo reads "BOX No. 014", which contradicts the brief and the kit's numbering (Box 01), and it would put a wrong number in an announcement of Box 01. Photo 3 is a good payoff shot but shows the harvest, not the announcement's setup, so it's the runner-up.

Half Acre Club sends one small growing project a month for $24. Box 01 is pea shoots in a takeout tub, ready to cut in about ten days. The box holds seeds, a soil puck and a printed card; you save the tub. Cancel anytime. Link in bio. You've got this.

#peashoots #windowsillgarden

notes.reason: The kit names the offer badge as the first choice for promos because price and 'cancel anytime' are the facts that move people. The brief asks for exactly those two, and nothing in it argues against the default.

It shows the pea shoots, the reused takeout tub and how little room it takes, which answers the 'I don't have the space' barrier. The kit calls this shot the test of the direction, and it has no yard or styled harvest. The cream area below the photo keeps room for the red badge as the only red element.

The card reads 'BOX No. 014', but pea shoots is Box 01 and the club is new, so the number contradicts the kit and implies a long history. The red box label and red circled step would also compete with the offer badge, and the kit allows one red element per post.
The first cut is a good payoff shot, but the red-striped towel adds red next to the badge. It also shows the result rather than the small-space setup, and the promo is about joining and the price.

notes.choice: One windowsill. One project a month.

slots.headline: Grow something small. Cancel anytime.
slots.subhead: A monthly box with one small growing project, made for people without a garden.
slots.caption: No garden? No problem. Every month, Half Acre Club sends one small growing project in a box. Cancel anytime, so it's easy to try. See the monthly price and join via the link in bio. #HalfAcreClub #growyourown

notes.reason: The intent is promo, and offer-badge is the only template built for promo. Its stamp can carry the price, which is what the brief says to lead with. There is no kit, so this rests on the template's best_for list.

The post sells the box, and this photo shows what a member receives: the soil puck, seed packet and planting card. Photo 2 carries a dated tape label (3/14) that would age the post. Photo 3 shows the payoff but not the product. The printed 'BOX No. 014' is incidental, so copy should not treat it as the price or offer.

The brief asks to lead with price and cancel-anytime, but no price was supplied and I can't invent one. The headline leads with the low commitment and the small, doable project instead. It is 37 characters, inside the 40 limit.

"Cancel anytime" is 14 characters and the badge allows 12, so I used a shorter phrase with the same meaning. The headline carries the exact wording. A price badge should replace this once the client confirms the monthly price.

notes.choice: A monthly box with one small growing project, made for people without a garden.
notes.reason: It says what arrives and who it's for, using only facts from the business description. It is 79 characters.
The goal is new members, so this is a direct, plain invitation to join. It is 19 characters.

notes.choice: Short caption repeating cancel anytime, pointing to the link in bio for the monthly price, with two light hashtags.
notes.reason: It sends readers to the link in bio for the price rather than stating a number I don't have. I left out any mention of a discount because the client said there isn't one.

notes.choice: No price anywhere in the copy
notes.reason: The art director's plan flagged that the price is missing. Adding a made-up figure would be a false claim, so the client needs to supply it and can add it to the badge or headline before posting.

slots.subhead: Not dripping, not dry. If water pools on top, wait a day.
slots.caption: How wet should the soil be for pea shoots? Think of a wrung-out sponge. Water until the soil feels damp all the way through, but not dripping and not dry. If water pools on top, leave it a day before you water again. Link in bio to see what's in this month's box.

Type-led takes no photo, and none of the three shows what the tip is about. Photo 2 shows the soil only through the tub's side and its tape label adds an unrelated date (3/14, Day 6). Photo 3 is about harvesting, and photo 1 is a box unboxing. Photo 1's card does show the circled 'wrung-out sponge' step, but it would only repeat the headline in small print.

notes.reason: The kit names the event card as the first choice for events because date and place must read at a glance. Nothing in the brief gives a reason to depart from it.

Bring your own, whether you're about to start your first tray or just curious how it works. Thursday, Nov 20 at 7pm ET on Instagram Live. Link in bio.

notes.reason: The brief's intent is event, and event-card is the template built for it, with the name, a large handwritten date, and the time and place in a clear hierarchy. Nothing in the brief gives a reason to use another template.

Event-card takes no photo, so none is chosen. Photo 3 (the cut) would have been the best fit for the topic, but photo 2 and photo 1 are tied to a specific box (Pea Shoots, Box No. 014, a 3/14 label), which could contradict a Nov 20 event. Skipping photos avoids that clash.
The event name is the headline, as the template notes say, and it matches the brief exactly.
